skills_considered.reason: The discovery ledger is a research surface another batch owns; this wave's question is patient provenance and counting, so findings are proposed through commit candidates instead of ledger edits.
No source in this group tests a therapy against a mechanism; forging hypotheses from single-patient drug histories would manufacture a lead.
No compound is proposed as a candidate; anti-seizure medication histories in case reports are clinical descriptions, not molecules for BLOCK-1 triage.
Scientists do not touch the four current files; changes are proposed as commit candidates for a later BATCH_COMMIT.
No proposed change narrows or reverses a consolidated baseline claim; the triples are published in the candidates for an auditor to run.

group_assessment.weighting: PubMed counts 2026-10-03: Schols L[au] 539 records, 2 intersecting WWOX (Mallaret 2014, co-authored, and this cohort). Neurogenetics group with exome pipeline; the WWOX family is the group's own previously published family.

field_density.note: This cohort is one of twelve consanguinity exome records naming WWOX; its WWOX family is not new.

multihop.note: All 50 references enumerated; ref 18 (Mallaret 2014) is the WWOX paper, confirmed by Table S1 ('this family is published (PMID: 24369382)'). Table 1's bracketed reference for the WWOX row ([24]) does not resolve to a WWOX paper in the reference list.

corpus_crossquery.note: FT-140 only. The 2026-09-21 receipt and triage state that the paper has zero WWOX variants; the XML Table 1 and Table S1 refute that.
